extracted.intended_audience: TeX/LaTeX users (mathematicians, category-theorists, document authors) choosing or using macro packages to typeset commutative diagrams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for selecting and using TeX/LaTeX macro packages to create commutative diagrams (from simple rectangular arrays to complex non‑planar diagrams). Covers technical, usability, installation, and output‑quality aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrow styles
rubrics_metrics.description: The arrows used in commutative diagrams often are of different shapes, tails, heads, and shaft styles (solid, dashed, dotted) to distinguish kinds of morphisms (monomorphisms, epimorphisms, isomorphisms, inclusions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A collection of built-in arrow shapes and shafts should be included; packages may provide facilities for defining new arrow styles by choosing combinations of tail, head, and shaft from a palette. Ability to define custom arrow styles is desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for diagonal/curved arrows and arbitrary slopes
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for diagonal arrows (various slopes), curved arrows, loops, parallel/adjoint arrows, and in some packages arbitrary slopes (often via PostScript rotation specials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary when distinguishing parallel morphisms or representing loops and non‑planar connections; some packages restrict to usual LaTeX slopes, others implement arbitrary slopes via PostScript. Curved arrows improve clarity and aesthetics and cannot always be eliminated by duplicating nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic stretching
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether arrows automatically stretch to meet their source and target nodes and/or to fit long labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic stretching may be appropriate for horizontal/vertical arrows but problematic for diagonals (may leave arrow too far from node). Degree of automatic stretching varies by package (see Appendix III examples); some packages stretch to meet nodes and labels, others do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagram fine-tuning (manual adjustment facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities for manual fine-tuning: moving labels and arrows, modifying arrow size, adjusting distance from source node to arrow start and from arrow end to target node, and setting per-row/column spacing parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fine-tuning is often required for complex diagrams due to limited slopes, arrow crossings, and label superimposition. Packages differ widely in fine-tuning support; per-row/column gap control is important for three‑dimensional perspective without adding empty rows/columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conception of underlying grid/array (cell model)
rubrics_metrics.description: How the array of cells underlying a diagram is conceived: either (a) one object and all departing morphisms in each non-empty cell, or (b) one object or one or more morphisms in each non-empty cell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement of extra cells for morphisms (option b) increases difficulty and code size; choice affects readability of source and ease of use. The array conception is a major determinant of ease of authoring diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Node/addressing schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: How coordinates for source and target nodes are specified: implicit in arrow name, absolute coordinates, coordinates relative to source cell, or symbolic (named) addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic addressing (naming nodes) is preferable for complex diagrams as it separates node arrangement from arrow specification. Absolute/relative addressing and implicit coordinates each have trade-offs for ease and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ease of use
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjective ease of use, depending on prior experience; includes array conception, addressing model, and degree of manual fine‑tuning required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two important aspects are (1) how the grid/array must be conceived (extra cells make usage harder), and (2) how many manual adjustments are required. Some packages let diagrams be input like ordinary math and need little tuning; others require per-node/arrow positioning and much effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation
rubrics_metrics.description: Complexity of installing the macro package and any accompanying fonts or files (single macro/style file vs. additional METAFONT fonts or PostScript dependencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most packages require dropping one file into the TeX search path; packages with special fonts (to get more diagonal slopes or arrow shapes) complicate installation and may require system admin or METAFONT support. Some distribute ready‑to‑use fonts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Range and quality of documentation available: from small text files to comprehensive user guides or book chapters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good documentation (examples, user guide, reference manual) greatly eases adoption. The paper rates documentation from 'scarce' to 'excellent' across packages and notes some have comprehensive guides while others have only brief manuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: User support and maintainership
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of author support, responsiveness to suggestions, and ongoing development/funding of the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors of many packages have been receptive and provide support; ongoing development and funded maintenance (e.g., XY‑pic) are positive signals for long‑term viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource requirements (computation, memory, typesetting time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount of TeX computations, memory words, file size, and processing time required to typeset diagrams; complex diagrams can be resource‑intensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because many packages implement drawing atop TeX, they may require many small segments and computations; Appendix IV compares main file sizes and time statistics (total and marginal times) measured on sample diagrams. Consider package size and processing time when choosing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability (licence and CTAN presence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the macro package is available via CTAN, and its licensing (public domain, free software, GPL, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reviewed packages can be found on CTAN and are either public domain or free software under terms such as the GPL; Appendix V lists CTAN directories and mirrors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility and convertibility between packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which diagrams can be converted among different macro packages, considering differences in construction approach, naming conventions, arrow styles, and slopes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macro packages are highly incompatible; conversion is nontrivial and may require rebuilding diagrams from scratch. Some packages (e.g., Paul Taylor's) provide emulation facilities. A common syntax/standard would ease portability.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEX format requirements and portability
rubrics_metrics.description: Which TeX formats the package runs on (plain TeX, LaTeX, AMS‑TeX, LAMS‑TeX) and any dependencies (picture environment, special fonts, amsmath, PostScript).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some packages only run under LaTeX (depend on picture env or fonts), others require AMS‑TeX or amsmath, and some run on plain TeX. Consider target document format and system availability before choosing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output quality (visual/readability/typographic quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjective assessment of the final diagram quality (clarity, aesthetics, correct placement of arrows and labels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output quality is subjective and should be judged using sample diagrams; packages vary in how nicely they typeset diagrams without manual adjustment. Author leaves this to reader evaluation with samples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability to produce complex diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability of the macro package to handle complex, non‑planar diagrams with many nodes, varied arrow shapes and slopes, labels, crossings, and three‑dimensional perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for symbolic addressing, arbitrary slopes, curved arrows, and extensive fine‑tuning facilities makes producing complex diagrams more feasible. Some packages restrict slope choices or limit items per cell, reducing capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntactic conventions and standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: The syntax used to specify diagrams (matrix‑like notation, shape composition primitives, named nodes) and the community discussion about adopting a common syntax (LATEX3 Research on Syntax for Commutative Diagrams).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntactic issues greatly influence user acceptance; a common agreed‑upon syntax would help portability. The paper describes an active discussion (1992–1993) and argues syntax is fundamental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design/readability principles for diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for designing readable diagrams: follow natural writing order (left→right, top→bottom), give depth to three‑dimensional diagrams (foreground slightly below background), and emphasize readability over purely formal arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good design improves communication; readability principles may conflict (e.g., top‑to‑bottom vs foreground/background), so use them as guidelines to craft clear diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: User interface and WYSIWYG/graphics tool support
rubrics_metrics.description: The interface for creating diagrams: textual matrix/command syntax versus the possibility of a drawing program (WYSIWYG) that can export to macro package languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While many argue for markup over WYSIWYG, a dedicated drawing program could let users design node/arc layouts with a mouse and export to multiple macro syntaxes, automating coordinate computation, slope choice, label placement, and fine‑tuning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to user errors and learning curve
rubrics_metrics.description: How robust a package is when users make common mistakes (omitting brackets, mistyping commands) and how quickly users learn to produce diagrams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper suggests measuring learning times and robustness; packages with clearer syntax and better error messages will be easier to learn and less error‑prone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of sample diagrams and example code
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of representative sample diagrams and code snippets showing how to implement typical and complex diagrams using the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample diagrams (Appendix I shows same diagram rendered by many packages) help users judge output quality and learn the package; presence of sample code in distributed docs is valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for defining mnemonic/addressing shortcuts
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to define mnemonics or macros for common arrow coordinates and frequently used structures to simplify source code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mnemonics ease writing diagrams (Spivak/LAMS‑TeX example). Symbolic addressing and coordinate mnemonics reduce error and improve maintainability of complex diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree to which package aids diagram quality (informative messages, guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the package provides informative messages or built‑in assistance that helps improve diagram quality or warns about layout problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper suggests evaluating how much each package helps users improve output quality (informative messages, suggestions). Packages that nudge towards better layouts reduce manual tuning.
